defects.source: PR #391 independent review (Codex P1, CodeRabbit Major) on 2026-08-30. The first correction for the API-only code-write ingress gap asserted prevention using a denylist of committer logins, emails and names. The Contents API and Git Data API let a caller supply any author and committer identity, so an API-only write evaded the denylist and could still reach hosted preflight success; the check also read only the tip, so a clone-authored tip concealed an API-written ancestor. A class represented as prevented recurred in review, so the prevention system itself was the defect.
defects.guard_boundary: candidate admission requires positive, exact-SHA-bound ingress proof for every commit in the pull request range, never absence of a denied identity and never the tip alone
defects.guard: verify_code_write_ingress_provenance() requires each commit in the PR commit range to carry a GitHub-verified signature (verified is True and reason == 'valid') from a signer allowlisted in docs/CODE_WRITE_POLICY.json. The signature is computed over the commit object, so the SHA is the signed identity: a proof cannot be detached, replayed onto a newer SHA, or supplied as Contents API or Git Data API commit metadata, and hosted CI success cannot substitute for it. The policy is read by the governance controller from the trusted default branch, so a candidate cannot widen its own allowlist or move its own attestation floor. Only the committer login is trusted for signer identity because a verified signature binds the committer email to the key owner; the author field carries no such binding. Commits reachable from the declared attested_from_commit floor predate the authority and are exempt, and three-dot comparison excludes only ancestors of that floor, so the exemption cannot be steered onto a later commit. Missing policy, an empty allowlist, unavailable or malformed range evidence, an unsigned commit, an unverified signature and an unauthorized signer all fail closed

defects.source: Issue #313 ADR 0034 Phase B hostile self-review: a transport-class lookup table mapped TIMEOUT directly to TIMEOUT_CONFIRMED_NO_DELIVERY, so a read timeout after the request was already on the wire would have been recorded as proven non-delivery and would then have authorized a retry that could duplicate a billable provider execution
defects.guard_boundary: Model Adapter transport-result classification and ModelAttemptOutcomeRecord construction
defects.guard: two independent boundaries, neither sufficient alone. classify_transport_result() resolves TIMEOUT and CONNECTION_FAILED from the transport's reported delivery certainty rather than from the failure class, so a proven non-delivery is required before TIMEOUT_CONFIRMED_NO_DELIVERY can be produced; and _REQUIRED_DELIVERY_CERTAINTY is enforced in ModelAttemptOutcomeRecord.__post_init__, so no code path anywhere can construct an outcome whose certainty contradicts its own semantics, alongside the paired invariant that an outcome with UNKNOWN certainty may never carry RETRY_REQUIRES_NEW_ATTEMPT. Transports report CONFIRMED_NOT_DELIVERED only for failures that provably precede request acceptance (connection refused, name resolution failure); a mid-flight reset stays uncertain

defects.source: Issue #313 ADR 0034 Phase B hostile self-review: a provider response is untrusted external content that may echo an API key, bearer token, or cookie irrespective of which durable categories are authorized, so per-category Source Handling authorization alone would have licensed persisting credential-bearing bytes and a hash derived from them
defects.guard_boundary: Model Adapter response capture, before ProviderResponseArtifact construction
defects.guard: response_content_credential_risk() runs as a second, independent gate after the per-category durability decision and before the canonical record is constructed, so the boundary is structural rather than a post-hoc scan of an already-built record. On refusal the artifact records RESPONSE_EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE_CREDENTIAL_RISK with a stable reason code and carries no bytes, hash, measured size, or content-derived identity, because a digest of credential-bearing material is itself a credential-derived representation; the transport outcome is still recorded. The gate is shape-based rather than keyword-based, so an ordinary model answer discussing authentication remains retainable and the guard does not reject canonically valid output (PRH-009)

defects.source: Issue #313 ADR 0034 Phase B hostile self-review: prepare_attempt accepted attempt_ordinal > 1 with only a predecessor attempt identity, so a caller could prepare and dispatch a second attempt after an uncertain first attempt whose request the provider may already have accepted. Recurrence on PR #314 independent review (Codex P1): the first guard derived its decision from the caller-supplied predecessor ModelAttemptOutcomeRecord, so a fabricated record naming the predecessor and claiming RETRY_REQUIRES_NEW_ATTEMPT defeated the gate entirely while the repository held an uncertain outcome or none at all — the prior hardening was insufficient because it checked the shape of the evidence instead of resolving the authority
defects.guard_boundary: ModelAdapterService.prepare_attempt, before any authority resolution or durable write
defects.guard: a retry requires the predecessor attempt's own DURABLE outcome, resolved from persistence via authoritative_outcome() strict-known at the new attempt's cutoff and following the supersession chain, checked before Source Handling is resolved and before anything durable exists. A caller-supplied record is evidence only: it is compared against the durable one and a mismatch is rejected, never used in its place — the same treatment prepare_attempt already gives a caller-supplied Source Handling decision and the ADR 0033 persistence invariant requires generally. Retry is admitted only when the durable outcome's retry_authorization is RETRY_REQUIRES_NEW_ATTEMPT, which derive_retry_authorization() grants only where the transport proved non-delivery or the provider established it rejected the request instead of executing it; an attempt with no durable outcome is uncertain and blocks retry. An authorized retry still gets a new attempt, cutoff, Source Handling resolution, handoff, and idempotency key, and terminal_outcome_exists() prevents re-dispatching an attempt that already has an outcome

defects.source: Issue #313 ADR 0034 Phase B hostile self-review: a transport whose send() took only a request could be called directly, producing a real provider invocation with no durable attempt, no handoff consumption, and no attributable outcome
defects.guard_boundary: provider transport send contract and Model Adapter dispatch path
defects.guard: every send requires a DispatchAuthorization, which refuses construction without a module-private mint held only by the Model Adapter and is created only after consume_handoff_once has already claimed the handoff by compare-and-set, so a dispatch authorization cannot exist unless a durable attempt and an unconsumed handoff existed a moment earlier. The adapter additionally binds the dispatch to exactly the profile the attempt was prepared against and to exactly the transport identity and version that profile names, so there is no selection input and no supported path by which a different transport, profile, or provider can be substituted

defects.source: PR #314 independent review (Codex P1): ModelAdapterService.dispatch used the caller-supplied EvidencePromptArtifact's content to build the wire request without binding it to the prepared attempt, so a substituted prompt could be transmitted while durable lineage still named the prepared one. EvidencePromptArtifact.artifact_id excludes content and the dataclass does not self-verify its declared hash, so an identity check alone would still have admitted arbitrary bytes under the prepared identity
defects.guard_boundary: Model Adapter dispatch, before the handoff is consumed
defects.guard: the payload whose bytes reach the provider is bound to the attempt on both axes before any send: prompt_artifact.artifact_id must equal attempt.prompt_artifact_id, and _verify_prompt_content_matches_declared_identity() must confirm that sha256(content) equals the declared content_hash and that the encoded length equals the declared measured_size_bytes. Identity equality alone proves only that the claims match; the second check proves the bytes behind those claims do too. Both run before consume_handoff_once, so a refusal transmits nothing and leaves the handoff unconsumed. The general rule this encodes: where a canonical identity is derived from declared metadata rather than from the payload itself, a consumer that transmits or persists that payload must re-verify the payload against the declaration rather than trusting the identity

defects.source: PR #314 independent review (Codex P2): strict_known_response_artifact ordered ascending with LIMIT 1, so once append_outcome admitted a superseding correction carrying revised response evidence, every later strict-known read returned the original artifact permanently and the correction was invisible
defects.guard_boundary: Model Adapter persistence strict-known historical reads
defects.guard: authoritative_outcome() resolves the head of the supersession chain — the outcome that no other outcome KNOWN AT THE SAME CUTOFF supersedes — and strict_known_response_artifact() returns the artifact attached to that governing outcome, falling back to the most recent earlier artifact when the correction records no new response evidence. Both remain strict-known, so a correction recorded after the cutoff does not retroactively govern an earlier read and the superseded original is preserved rather than overwritten. The general rule: wherever a record family admits append-only corrections, a historical read must follow the supersession chain, because neither the earliest row nor a blind latest row is the authoritative one

defects.source: PR #314 independent review (CodeRabbit, Major): append_outcome cross-checked attempt, handoff, and profile lineage between an outcome and its response artifact but never compared outcome.response_artifact_identity with the artifact's own computed identity, and never rejected an outcome claiming a response-artifact identity while supplying no artifact. defects.guard_boundary: Model Adapter persistence linkage verification in append_outcome
defects.guard: append_outcome verifies the outcome's declared response_artifact_identity against the supplied artifact's own computed identity, and rejects an outcome that declares such an identity while no artifact is supplied; both absent remains valid. The general rule: where one durable record names another by a content-derived identity, persistence must verify that the named identity is the identity of the record actually being written, not merely that the two objects agree on their other lineage fields

defects.source: PR #314 independent review (CodeRabbit, Minor) and hostile self-review: a transport may report a result-class/delivery-certainty pairing the outcome family forbids (for example RESPONSE_RECEIVED with UNKNOWN certainty). defects.guard_boundary: Model Adapter dispatch, every path after the handoff is consumed
defects.guard: once a send has occurred, every inconsistency is recorded rather than raised. dispatch validates the classified outcome/certainty pairing against _REQUIRED_DELIVERY_CERTAINTY and records INTERNAL_ADAPTER_ERROR with honest UNKNOWN certainty instead of letting record construction raise, joining the existing fallbacks for a non-canonical transport result and a transport identity or version mismatch. The general rule: after an external invocation, an adapter-internal contradiction is itself evidence and must be persisted with truthful uncertainty; raising would destroy the only record that the invocation happened

defects.source: PR #314 independent review (CodeRabbit, Major): _record_capture_persistence_failure hardcoded execution_evidence PROVIDER_RETURNED_COMPLETION, but that path runs whenever any response text was captured, including a MALFORMED_RESPONSE whose transport observation is UNKNOWN. The record therefore claimed the provider returned a completion when the transport had established no such thing, contradicting the truthful-classification invariant this phase exists to uphold. Separately, a malformed numeric profile parameter made body construction fail inside transport.send after the handoff was consumed, and was recorded as uncertain delivery even though no request byte had been offered
defects.guard_boundary: Model Adapter outcome construction and transport-level result normalization
defects.guard: every recorded axis carries the observation rather than an assumption in either direction. _record_capture_persistence_failure takes the transport's observed execution_evidence through as a parameter (UNKNOWN where no result exists) instead of asserting a completion, and the OpenAI transport converts a request-body construction failure into CONFIRMED_NOT_DELIVERED with NO_EXECUTION_ESTABLISHED, because a body that was never built means no byte was ever offered. The general rule: an outcome field must record what was established, never the strongest or the safest value that would fit -- overstating certainty and overstating uncertainty are both untruthful

defects.source: PR #354 independent Codex P1 and CodeRabbit Major security reviews on 2026-08-27
defects.guard_boundary: Smart Prompt Machine automation-envelope issuance and transport boundary
defects.guard: PromptAutomationEnvelope carries an Ed25519 signature over the exact seven non-content lineage claims. HUNTER_PROMPT_AUTOMATION_SIGNING_KEY is issuer-only private key material; network-capable verifier workers capture HUNTER_PROMPT_AUTOMATION_VERIFYING_KEY once in an immutable PromptAutomationVerifier during trusted bootstrap, so later os.environ mutation cannot change the issuer trust root, and missing or malformed key material fails closed. SmartPromptMachine is the supported issuer, and PromptAutomationDispatcher binds the envelope once, requires its exact canonical type, and calls the bound verifier before constructing any external payload, so neither a subtype nor a changing request property can override verification. Its dispatch authorization context is closure-owned and no importable ContextVar can mint it. The signature is excluded from the transport mapping, while hostile tests reject prompt text, token values, caller-supplied signatures, verifier overrides, post-verification envelope swaps, mutable-verifier bypasses, caller-writable dispatch context, private-key-free n8n verification, and cross-process verification failures

defects.source: Issue #403 governed ChatGPT/trusted-connector code-write ingress, 2026-08-31
defects.guard_boundary: Connector code-write authorization and exact-head candidate admission
defects.guard: docs/CODE_WRITE_POLICY.json connector_write_ingress is the only grant that can authorize a non-clone code write, and it is read by the governance controller from the trusted default branch so a candidate cannot grant itself ingress. hunter_connector_write_ingress rejects, fail-closed, a disabled or unbound grant, an unauthorized writer, a writer without the granted capability, a non-branch or protected-branch target (so a direct main write is unrepresentable), a branch whose name does not bind the one declared governing Issue, a base ref other than the authorized base, a base commit that is not the exact observed base tip, and any changed path that is prohibited or outside the granted scope -- including the hooks, workflows, scripts, and policy files that bind the ingress itself. It shares one path-scope semantic with the workflow state gate rather than defining a second one, and admission re-uses the authorizer's own check_scope. The base tip is never caller-supplied: it is resolved from trusted repository state at authorization time and re-checked immediately before the write is applied, so a stale caller cannot certify its own staleness and an authorization cannot be applied after the base advances. Because a verified signature from an allowlisted account proves only who wrote a commit and never that the write crossed the authorizer, an authorized decision mints a canonical claim set whose authorization_id is a SHA-256 over exactly those claims; the writer commits it to the candidate head, and hunter_governance_review_v2 re-derives every claim from trusted repository and pull-request evidence -- branch, base, fork point, governing Issue derived from the branch itself, committer of every attested commit, and the trusted changed-file list re-scoped against the grant. A connector-namespace branch without a receipt, a receipt outside the namespace, a receipt understating the changed files, or one minted for another branch, Issue, or fork point all fail admission however green the hosted statuses are. The connector authenticates as an account that is also a clone-capable signer, so committer login cannot separate the channels and identity disjointness would only make the grant unbindable; the channels are separated by evidence instead: the grant may not declare pre-push equivalence, an active grant must declare that trusted hosted exact-head proof is required for all candidates or the loader and guard refuse it, and while the grant is active a verified signature alone admits nothing -- every code-changing range additionally requires the trusted hosted exact-head canonical preflight status for that exact head and PR, in addition to the existing exact-head branch preflight. That status is minted only by the trusted default-branch controller against the exact candidate SHA, so no writer on either channel can produce it. Hostile tests cover arbitrary writer rejection, stale base including a self-consistent stale pair and a base that advances before application, Issue scope mismatch, direct-main attempt, writes outside the connector namespace, missing/prohibited/out-of-scope/understated paths, a missing or forged authorization receipt, receipts replayed onto another branch or a newer head, missing and failed hosted preflight, proof bound to another PR, superseded exact-head proof, a shared connector/clone identity, and an active grant that drops the hosted-proof requirement

defects.source: Issue #405 standing owner-directed ChatGPT governance maintenance, 2026-09-01
defects.guard_boundary: Governance-maintenance capability scope, root-of-trust floor, and same-candidate self-escalation
defects.guard: Removing the Issue #403 governance prohibitions to unblock owner-authorized ADR lifecycle work would have let the connector rewrite the authority that evaluates it, so the capability is added as a separate grant under a three-layer scope model read only from the trusted default branch. connector_write_ingress.root_of_trust_paths is a floor no capability may write and no named scope may unblock: the push boundary, the hosted workflows, the canonical gate chain's own scripts, the connector authorizer, the governance/admission controllers, the merge-readiness controller, the shared scope and transport primitives, the packaging and tooling pins, and the policy itself. hunter_connector_write_ingress checks that floor before any capability scope and for every capability. The governance-maintenance capability reuses the ordinary prohibited scope as its closed default, so it grants nothing on its own; a prohibited path opens only when a named scope in governance_maintenance_scopes unblocks it AND the governing Issue -- derived from the trusted branch name, never from the receipt -- holds that scope in governance_maintenance_authorizations. Scope-to-floor overlap is checked entry-to-entry in BOTH directions, because a broad 'docs/' entry is not itself a root-of-trust path but covers one, and no scope may reach outside its capability's allowed paths, so scopes can only re-open what the closed default shut. Self-escalation is closed three independent ways: the policy is unreachable through the ingress; an authorized decision pins grant_fingerprint, a SHA-256 over every authorization-relevant grant field, which hunter_governance_review_v2 re-derives from the default branch so a receipt minted under any other grant version is stale; and the controller parses the candidate head's own policy with the same rules and refuses any connector candidate whose head widens the grant -- a new capability, writer, allowed path, dropped prohibition, dropped floor entry, new or widened scope, new or widened Issue authorization, or a newly activated grant -- while deliberately permitting narrowing. hunter_defect_prevention_preflight derives the required floor rather than enumerating it: it starts from the canonical gate chain's own commands, the scripts .githooks/pre-push runs, and the scripts run by any workflow whose declared permissions grant statuses, checks, or pull-requests write -- so a workflow that can mint or clear a merge-gating signal is selected by that capability rather than by name -- and then follows both imports and literal scripts/...py references transitively, because a dependency of a decision is part of that decision. Only the non-Python authorities that cannot be reached by following entrypoints are static. An unreadable or unparseable source is a derivation error, never a silently shorter floor, and ordinary automation that mints no gating signal is deliberately not swept in, since over-blocking is itself a defect. Review of PR #406 found the first form of this guard derived the floor from the gate chain alone, so a later policy could drop scripts/hunter_pre_push.py -- the push boundary's own implementation, reached only by the hook shelling out to it -- and then unblock it through an Issue-authorized scope with both the guard and the loader silent; the derived closure closes that gap at its root rather than by adding one name to a list. The guard also rejects a capability that does not close the floor, a scope that unblocks it, an authorization naming an unknown scope, and a governance-maintenance capability that does not require per-Issue authorization. Hostile tests cover same-PR widening with and without a valid receipt, root-of-trust mutation under every capability, an unauthorized Issue, an authorized Issue reaching outside its scopes, a stale base, a receipt minted under an older grant, a receipt replayed onto another branch, missing and wrong-PR hosted exact-head proof, and the unchanged Issue #403 ordinary write path

defects.source: Issue #409 connector admission blocked as unsigned on PR #408, 2026-09-01
defects.guard_boundary: Exact-head candidate admission ingress-channel decision
defects.guard: Issues #403/#405 authorize connector-written candidates without treating that channel as local pre-push proof. hunter_governance_review_v2 decides the ingress channel from trusted evidence before applying its proof contract: ordinary clone-path commits retain the verified-signature requirement across the applicable range, while connector-origin admission re-derives the exact-head receipt against the trusted grant, branch, Issue, merge base, path scope, root-of-trust floor, grant fingerprint, and same-PR anti-self-escalation boundary. The connector writer is authenticated for every commit in the connector range from a trusted push-event Hunter / Pre-PR Preflight workflow run for that commit SHA and the exact PR head branch; missing evidence fails closed, and PR authorship plus unsigned committer metadata are never identity proof. The committer listing remains only a narrowing consistency check, so forged authorized metadata cannot conceal a foreign ancestor writer. Canonical v4 receipt changes distinguish addition, modification, removal, and rename: resulting blobs bind additions/modifications, absence binds removals rather than GitHub's base-blob SHA, and source plus destination plus resulting blob bind renames. Admission preserves status and previous_filename, so same-path mutation, deletion, rename, rename-plus-modification, or protected-source rename requires fresh authorization or fails scope. The hosted upgrade proof is not accepted from context and success alone: its publisher must be github-actions[bot], its canonical target must resolve inside this repository to Hunter / Trusted Preflight Upgrade, and that completed successful pull_request_target run must bind the exact PR and exact head. Hostile tests cover different exact-head and ancestor push actors despite forged authorized committer metadata, missing ancestor push evidence, mixed writers, same-path mutation, deletion using the base blob SHA, protected-source rename, rename-plus-modification, receipt-path rename concealment, forged push-user statuses, wrong App/workflow/PR/head proof, and the preserved base/Issue/branch/path/root-of-trust/signature boundaries.

defects.source: Issue #390 PR #414 independent owner review, 2026-09-05
defects.guard_boundary: Issue authorization ingress at the production execution composition root
defects.guard: A deterministic identity derived from a document's own claims proves internal consistency, never provenance: every field hunter-issue-agent-authorization-v1 covers -- repository, Issue number, URL, title, body, owner login, governed label, updated_at -- is public on an owner-authored Issue, so any caller who can reach the credential-free issuer endpoint can recompute the digest and mint a self-consistent document. Comparing authorized_by to configured owner text compares attacker-chosen text to a constant and proves nothing either. The correcting change adds authentication as a separate outer schema rather than redefining the canonical payload named by accepted ADR 0036 s7: hunter-issue-agent-signed-authorization-v1 carries that exact payload verbatim plus a domain-separated Ed25519 issuer signature over the whole payload, including its authorization_id and schema_version. The workflow that actually observes the owner's issues:labeled event holds the private key as a repository secret; the composition root verifies with a public key captured once at trusted bootstrap, before the ledger claim, before durable intake and before any dispatch. The envelope is the only executable form, so a bare unsigned payload is refused on the outer field set and has no execution path. The split is asymmetric on purpose: the execution side holds only the public half, so it can verify an owner authorization and can never mint one, the keypair is distinct from the Smart Prompt automation keypair, and a later environment mutation cannot move the trust root. A downstream content-classification gate is not a substitute: Source Handling governs whether an exact document scope may be processed, so for any Issue whose exact content already carries published FACT/POLICY/FIELD_CATEGORY_REGISTRY authority it admits a forged payload as readily as a genuine one.

families.title: untrusted-temporal-authority
families.invariant: Time that decides admission, ordering or cutoff is sampled from trusted repository/runtime authority, never accepted from the caller or sampled before the transaction that it orders.

applicability.rationale: Runtime authority code is where caller-supplied timestamps become admission or ordering decisions.

prevention.mechanism: Adversarial review of every timestamp that reaches an admission, ordering or cutoff decision, plus the PR #411 regressions that pin trusted-cutoff and post-acquisition sampling.

families.title: transaction-snapshot-inconsistency
families.invariant: A read that validates history and the write that depends on it observe one explicit snapshot; no decision is made across two independently-taken views.

applicability.rationale: Repository and persistence code is where a validating read and its dependent write can drift apart.

prevention.mechanism: Adversarial review of every validate-then-write sequence for a single explicit snapshot, plus the PR #411 snapshot regression.

families.title: logical-identity-reuse
families.invariant: A caller-supplied payload cannot select, override or reuse a repository-assigned logical identity, and an authorization bound to one identity is not reusable for another.

applicability.rationale: Persistence and authorization code is where a caller-chosen identifier can displace an assigned one.

prevention.mechanism: Adversarial review of every identity assignment reachable from a caller payload, plus the PR #411 identity-override regression.

families.title: schema-fail-closed-incompleteness
families.invariant: An unknown, absent or partially-declared authority value fails closed; absence is never read as permission and a schema is never satisfied by an incomplete declaration.

applicability.rationale: Schema and authority-resolution code is where an incomplete declaration can be read as a permissive default.

prevention.mechanism: Adversarial review of every authority lookup for its absent/unknown branch, plus the PR #411 explicit-availability and permissive-default regressions.

families.title: nested-metadata-persistence-bypass
families.invariant: A restriction that excludes content from durable persistence cannot be bypassed by nesting that content inside metadata, a prepared artifact, or any other secondary surface.

applicability.rationale: Persistence code is where a governed exclusion can be defeated by a secondary carrying surface.

prevention.mechanism: Adversarial review of every durable write surface against the governing restriction, plus the PR #411 metadata-nesting and credential-surface regressions.

families.title: monotonicity-and-restart-instability
families.invariant: Ordering guarantees survive a frozen clock, a process restart and a crash-retry; a repeated or non-advancing external clock never produces a non-monotonic admitted order.

applicability.rationale: Ordering and persistence code is where restart and clock behaviour decide admitted order.

prevention.mechanism: Adversarial review of every ordering guarantee under frozen-clock and restart conditions, plus the PR #411 monotonicity regression.

families.title: authorization-replay
families.invariant: An authorization binds the exact operation and content it was minted for; it cannot be replayed onto a different operation, a different path, or different resulting content.

applicability.rationale: Authorization, ingress and persistence code is where a valid proof can be re-aimed at another target.

prevention.mechanism: The connector authorization identity is a SHA-256 over the exact claim set including per-file operation and resulting blob, and the trusted controller re-derives every claim from trusted evidence.

families.title: tamper-and-history-forgery
families.invariant: Repository-owned evidence is bound to its own content, so a hand-edited or forged artifact is detectable rather than merely implausible.

applicability.rationale: Evidence artifacts and the controllers that read them are where forgery has to be structurally detectable.

prevention.mechanism: Every repository-owned evidence artifact carries a digest over exactly its own claims, re-derived by the reader before any claim is believed.

families.title: connector-provenance-evidence-lifecycle
families.invariant: A channel that is authorized to write is granted a proof it can actually produce, and the proof authenticates the writer rather than restating caller-chosen metadata.

applicability.rationale: Ingress and admission code is where an authorized channel can be handed an unsatisfiable proof obligation.

prevention.mechanism: Candidate admission decides the write channel from trusted evidence first and only then requires that channel's own proof; the writer is authenticated from push-event workflow runs.

families.title: writer-identity-not-authorization-bound
families.invariant: Every commit in the governed range carries an author and a committer that each independently resolve to the same authorization-bound writer identity; agent attribution lives in trailers and never in identity.

applicability.rationale: Any change published through the repository-local push boundary is governed by the writer binding.

prevention.mechanism: scripts/hunter_pre_push.py validates the governed fork-point..HEAD range against the canonical writer_identity_binding before any remote mutation, and names the exact mismatched provenance claim.

families.title: stranded-intermediate-commit-evidence
families.invariant: A valid multi-commit candidate cannot strand an intermediate commit without admissible evidence, and no manual rewind or force-push is ever required solely to manufacture per-commit evidence.

applicability.rationale: Admission and push-boundary code is where an evidence model can make a valid commit permanently inadmissible.

prevention.mechanism: Range-level provenance: the authenticated push of the exact head publishes every commit the pull request lists, while an ancestor carrying its own authenticated push by a different actor still blocks.

families.title: stale-receipt-published
families.invariant: A receipt is the final mutation of the candidate that writes it: any later content change invalidates it, a stale receipt never reaches the remote, and a receipt inherited unchanged from the base branch is never read as a claim about a later candidate.

applicability.rationale: Any candidate that carries an authorization receipt is governed by receipt freshness.

prevention.mechanism: The push boundary re-derives the governed change set from git and refuses to publish a head whose own receipt no longer binds it, or a rename onto a governance evidence path. Applicability is derived from the change set: a receipt left on the base branch by a merged connector contribution is base state rather than this candidate's claim, and removing such a receipt is a retirement rather than a claim. Trusted admission applies the same rule on the ordinary path.

sources: PR #411 merged receipt on the default branch

families.title: ready-without-complete-hostile-review
families.invariant: A candidate is admitted for review only when exact-head-bound repository-owned state proves the complete base->HEAD range was hostile-reviewed against the governing Issue acceptance criteria and every applicable recurring-defect family, with no unresolved blocking finding.

applicability.rationale: Every candidate that changes repository content a reviewer would have to reason about is governed by the pre-ready hostile review requirement. Dependency manifests (requirements/, the root lockfiles and pyproject.toml) are deliberately outside this scope: a dependency-only candidate has no diff for a hostile pass to review, and demanding one would block every automated dependency update behind an artifact its author cannot produce -- a false-positive merge blockage, which is itself a defect.

prevention.mechanism: Candidate admission re-derives the base, the exact change set, the applicable families and the governing Issue's acceptance criteria from trusted evidence and refuses an absent, stale, incomplete or contested review; the controller returns the pull request to Draft. The acceptance criteria come from the owner-authored Issue rather than the artifact, so a review cannot measure itself against criteria it wrote for itself, and the Issue it names must be the Issue its branch binds.

families.title: pending-prerequisite-reported-as-failure
families.invariant: A hosted prerequisite that is still running publishes pending; only an invalid, absent, untrusted or wrongly-bound proof publishes failure. A head left pending is re-evaluated when the proof lands, so pending never becomes a way to stay Ready while unadmitted.

applicability.rationale: Admission and readiness controllers are where a transient state can be published as a defect.

prevention.mechanism: Candidate admission propagates a tri-state ingress verdict, so a running trusted proof is reported as pending rather than as a blocked candidate, and the candidate-admission controller subscribes to trusted-upgrade completion so a pending head is reconciled once the proof exists.

families.title: overclaimed-prevention-state
families.invariant: A defect family may claim an enforcement stage only when the evidence for that stage exists: a resolvable regression test above 'recorded', a resolvable machine guard above 'regression-tested', and a merge-gate boundary with explicit lifecycle enforcement evidence for 'prevented'.

applicability.rationale: The catalog and its validator are where a detection-only guard can be relabelled as prevention.

prevention.mechanism: scripts/hunter_defect_prevention_preflight.py structurally validates every family and refuses a stage the declared evidence does not support.
